text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, giving back some of the sharp gains it posted earlier this week when oil prices spiked to six-week highs following renewed Iran-U.S. military tensions. The stock had climbed nearly $7 from last Thursday through Tuesday as crude rose, but pulled back today even though oil remains elevated—suggesting some profit-taking after a strong run rather than a fresh negative catalyst.

The broader oil market remains supported by geopolitical risk (Iran-Saudi tensions, U.S. military involvement), and the Trump administration's Venezuela deal could eventually boost crude supply; but the stock's retreat after a four-day rally is a normal consolidation pattern when energy gains have been steep and fast.
